title: Markel's underwriting profit surges 55% as specialty insurer strips out reinsurance exit
full_text:
Markel Group’s core insurance operation delivered a 92% combined ratio and a 55% jump in underwriting profit in the nine months to September 30, 2026 - results that tell a materially different story from the headline premium figures.
Adjusted underwriting gross premium volume - which strips out the exited Global Reinsurance division and the transition of the Hagerty collector car book to a fronting arrangement - rose 9% in the third quarter and 10% year to date to $7.08 billion (all figures in USD). The unadjusted figures, down 9% for the quarter and 15% year to date, reflect those structural changes rather than any retreat from the specialty market.
Markel sold the renewal rights for its Global Reinsurance division in August 2025, placing it into run-off. From January 1, 2026, its Hagerty business - which covers collector cars and enthusiast vehicles - moved from an underwriting product to a fronting arrangement, changing how that premium volume is reported.
The fronting book itself grew 151% in the third quarter to $419 million, and 24% year to date to $2.29 billion - a figure that signals how actively Markel is building its MGA and delegated authority relationships. For brokers working in the specialty and E&S markets, the adjusted underwriting figures are the meaningful measure of Markel’s capacity and appetite.
Underwriting profit for the nine months reached $462.6 million, up 55% on the $298.8 million recorded in the same period of 2025. A 92% combined ratio - improving from 95% a year earlier and holding steady at 92% in the third quarter despite a three-point drag from the run-off Global Reinsurance book - indicates an operation underwriting profitably and with room to grow. Net investment income in the insurance segment rose 9% year to date to $694.4 million. Markel Insurance adjusted operating income for the nine months was $1.17 billion, up 19% year on year.
For brokers, a combined ratio at this level from a major specialty carrier matters: it points to an insurer with underwriting discipline and the financial headroom to maintain competitive appetite rather than pull back.
At group level, adjusted operating income - which excludes market movements in the equity portfolio - rose 14% in the third quarter to $707.4 million against $621 million in the same quarter of 2025. For the nine months, adjusted operating income was $1.64 billion, marginally down 2% on $1.68 billion in the prior year period, reflecting investment portfolio movements rather than operational performance. Operating revenues rose 6% in the quarter to $4.16 billion and 2% year to date to $11.73 billion.
Beyond insurance, the Industrial segment - which spans manufacturing businesses including bakery equipment, building supplies, and houseplants - posted 13% revenue growth in the quarter including 10% organic growth, with adjusted operating income up 29% to $131.1 million. The Financial segment delivered a 30% increase in adjusted operating income for the quarter to $80.1 million. The Consumer and Other segment saw adjusted operating income rise 80% in the quarter to $31.2 million.
Markel repurchased $315 million of its own shares in the third quarter and $685 million year to date, with shares outstanding down 10% over five years to 12.25 million - a consistent signal of management confidence in long-term intrinsic value growth.
Markel measures itself over five-year cycles rather than quarters. Average adjusted operating income over the five years to Q3 2026 was $1.96 billion, compared to $838 million over the prior five-year period - a trajectory that reflects both the scale of the insurance operation and the compounding effect of its diversified business model.
Chairman and CEO Tom Gayner said: “We build Markel to relentlessly compound value over the long-term, by serving our customers and policyholders, owning businesses with staying power, underwriting with discipline, and reinvesting patiently through cycles. Our third quarter results demonstrate we continue to do exactly that. Markel Insurance increased profitability, our Industrial, Financial, and Consumer and Other businesses delivered strong returns, and we continued to deploy capital where we believe it creates the most long-term value.”
